newsitem.title: GERMANY: Dasa wants new Airbus with full structure.
newsitem.headline: Dasa wants new Airbus with full structure.

text.p: The German partner in Europe's Airbus consortium said on Wednesday it still wanted to turn the loose partnership into a complete corporate entity, even though the French partner sought a looser structure.

Daimler-Benz Aerospace AG (DASA), a unit of car maker Daimler-Benz AG, also said an integrated organisation having design and production facilities was a goal the partners had agreed earlier this year.

"The memorandum of understanding signed by the partners says they will hold talks to find a way to achieve a complete corporation," Dasa spokesman Christian Poppe told Reuters on Wednesday. "That is completely clear."

DASA, which like France's Ste Nationale Industrielle Aerospatiale owns 37.9 percent of Airbus, wanted Airbus to emerge with a "complete structure that manages everything from development to product support," Poppe said.
The partners were still discussing a final agreement, he said.

The memorandum of understanding said the partners had agreed to study ways of transferring assets, including factories and design offices, to the new Airbus, as a first step to a wider integration of European civil and defence activities.

The future shape of Airbus was thrown into question last week when the chairman of Aerospatiale said the Airbus partners had agreed that Airbus would have "management mandates" over factories and design centres but would not own them.
British Aerospace Plc, which has a 20 percent stake in Airbus, has said it remains committed to the objectives of the memorandum and wanted Airbus to control its own assets.
Spain's Construcciones Aeronauticas SA (Casa) owns 4.2 percent of Airbus.
